summary: RetireMentorship iteration-4 backend verification (books/magazines/videos CPT endpoints + regressions). All 28 pytest cases passed (28/28, 100%). New coverage in TestBooksMagazinesVideos: (1) GET /api/books returns exactly 2 seed items with titles {'3D Retirement Income','Tax Saving Strategies'} and required fields id/slug/title/excerpt/type=='book'; (2) GET /api/books/book-3d-retirement-income → 200 with correct title; (3) GET /api/books/book-tax-saving-strategies → 200 with correct title; (4) GET /api/books/does-not-exist → 404; (5) GET /api/magazines → 200 with empty [] (WP CPT unregistered); (6) GET /api/videos?limit=5 → 200 with 1..5 items each type=='video'. Regressions all green: /api/wp/home-feed exposes hero/latest/videos/trending/tip, /api/wp/latest-modified returns non-null ISO modified + int id, /api/admin/leads → 401 without key & 200 with X-Admin-Key rm_admin_ChangeMe_2026, /api/wp/categories non-empty, /api/wp/posts?search=medicare returns >=1. Total wall time 17.4s under pytest-xdist (2 workers).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py list_books() falls back to hardcoded BOOK_FALLBACK when WP CPT returns []. This is intentional per spec, but note that transient WP 429/network errors will also produce [] and silently trigger the seed fallback rather than surfacing an upstream error. Consider distinguishing 'empty' from 'failed' before falling back.

server.py get_book() only tries WP when book_id.isdigit(); if you later mint numeric WP CPT ids AND keep the seed slug-based ids, a WP 429 will silently return seed data for that same slug. Fine for now, but document the precedence.

server.py list_videos() derives videos from the /posts endpoint. Currently retirementorship.com returns at least one YouTube-embedded post so the endpoint returns a non-empty list, but this is dependent on upstream content — if a stretch of posts contain no embeds, the endpoint could legitimately return [] and there is no test guard for that scenario.

server.py _fetch_cpt() swallows all exceptions and returns []. Combined with wp_get()'s internal fallbacks this creates two layers of silent failure. Add structured logging with a distinct 'cpt_missing' vs 'cpt_error' marker for observability.

server.py BOOK_FALLBACK is a module-level mutable list; harmless today but if any code path ever calls .append/.pop on it (e.g., a future admin CRUD) state will leak across requests. Freeze it or return copies from list_books().
server.py transform_post() and _transform_cpt() are ~80% duplicate logic; consolidate into a single helper that takes an optional 'type' arg.
server.py (carried over from iter-3): wp_get() line ~68 dict-vs-list default heuristic using path.endswith(tuple(f'/{i}' for i in range(10))) is fragile; safer to accept an explicit default param.
server.py transform_post() still does not guard against WP error dicts (e.g., {'code':'rest_post_invalid_id',...}); an invalid post id returns a 200 with mostly-null fields instead of 404.
seed_data_creation: None — books tests validate the hardcoded BOOK_FALLBACK seeds already baked into server.py.
